messages:
zoe: Quick heads-up: ran some field tests with FP8 on long multi-turn customer support prompts. A small slice shows hallucination spikes late in sequence. Brainstorm: build a 'fallback orchestrator' that can do token-level rollback or speculatively run a higher-precision continuation when a risk signal appears. Thoughts?

dmitri: Token-level rollback sounds pricey. How would we detect the risky token without re-running large chunks?

zana: Risk detection could be incremental: monitor logit distribution for each generated token. If we detect a sudden collapse (e.g., top1 prob > 0.9 and entropy drop), mark that token as risky and trigger speculative re-generation from last safe checkpoint.

sasha: Checkpointing frequency matters. Creating KV checkpoints every token is impossible. Maybe checkpoint every K tokens (e.g., 8), and for tokens between checkpoints we keep lightweight diffs to allow local rollback.

dmitri: Or we use speculative continuation: when signal hits, concurrently start a high-precision worker to produce the remaining tokens while letting FP8 finish. If FP8 result deviates beyond threshold, swap. That avoids rollback but uses extra compute sometimes.

zoe: That fits with SLO tradeoffs: extra compute vs worst-case bad outputs. We should make this pluggable per-tenant: e.g., enterprise legal customers prefer conservative mode (speculative + high-precision), freemium uses default FP8 with post-hoc validation.

zana: Cache reuse question: if speculative path runs at FP16, can it reuse FV cache? Need cache snapshot portability. Idea: maintain a canonical float32 cache format for snapshotting only when spec requested. Regular path still uses compressed caches.

sasha: That's a memory vs latency trade. Snapshotting to float32 on suspect events may be slow. Alternative: rehydrate compressed cache to FP16 on the speculative worker, paying CPU cost but avoiding float32 size.

dmitri: Telemetry/observability: we must log decision events: trigger_type, trigger_token_index, pre_trigger_signature, model_version, route_taken, cost_delta_ms, cost_delta_flops. Also surface to customers for billing transparency.

zoe: Agreed. Also we need offline labeling. We'll take shadow runs where we run FP8 + FP16 in parallel on a sampled traffic stream and compute a per-token divergence heatmap. Use that to train a small failure predictor.

zana: About thresholds: different models and prompt shapes behave differently. We'll expose per-model configuration for detector sensitivity with bounded knobs: sensitivity (false positive rate target), budget (max speculative rate), and fallback strategy (speculative/high-precision/annotate-only).

sasha: Ops implications: speculative runs inflate GPU utilization unpredictably. Need admission control: e.g., global speculative budget and per-instance burst allowance. If budget exhausted, revert to annotate-only fallback so we don't OOM or impact other tenants.

dmitri: For billing, charge based on actual compute used. Speculative work charged separately and flagged in invoice. Must add per-request metadata to correlate.

zoe: UX idea: request-level flags: "precision_policy": ["auto","prefer_high","no_speculate"], and responses include "speculation": "none|executed|throttled", "speculation_cost_usd": "0.00012", "reason": "entropy-collapse@token:34".

zana: Implementation plan: 1) prototype detector (heuristic) + lightweight speculative worker that consumes a cache snapshot (ETA 2w), 2) run shadow logging on 1% traffic to build labels and calibrate (ETA 3w), 3) RFC for orchestrator & quota model (ETA 1w after data).

sasha: QA: add stress tests simulating high speculative rates to see cross-tenant impact and failure modes. Also run degradation eval to quantify when swapping helps versus when it's noisy.

dmitri: Edge case: long-context generation where spec worker cannot catch up before completion. In that case, we should prefer checkpointed rollback strategy. We'll document heuristics: if remaining tokens < X, rollback; else speculate.

ops-bot: Action items captured in project 'precision-fallback': zoe/dmitri/ana/sasha assigned. Sprint target next iteration. :white_check_mark:

zoe: Excellent. I'll create the proto branch with detector heuristics + lightweight speculative worker and ping for review. Thanks!
